The lower half of the figure gives the placement positions: the first row is three adjacent rectangles I, II, III; the second row has IV and V below I and II respectively. Therefore the contact relationships are that the right side of I touches the left side of II, the right side of II touches the left side of III, the bottom side of I touches the top side of IV, the bottom side of II touches the top side of V, and the right side of IV touches the left side of V. C's right side 7 equals A's left side 7, so C can be on the left of A; A's right side 4 equals E's left side 4, so A can be on the left of E; E's right side 9 equals C's left side 9, so E can be on the left of C; D's right side 3 equals B's left side 3, so D can be on the left of B. From the position diagram, note the required contacts: I-right with II-left, II-right with III-left, I-bottom with IV-top, II-bottom with V-top, and IV-right with V-left. Build the directed horizontal matches by equating right-side numbers to left-side numbers: C can go left of A, A can go left of E, E can go left of C, and D can go left of B. Then test the only top-row chain that can also support the lower row: C-A-E gives I=C, II=A, III=E. Check verticals: C bottom 2 matches D top 2 for IV, A bottom 8 matches B top 8 for V, and D right 3 matches B left 3. All contacts work, so position I is C.

Test each rectangle’s right and bottom numbers against available left and top numbers.
